hops.rationale: The passages directly state the Data Center growth drivers for NVIDIA's fiscal 2024 10-K. Passage 110 gives Data Center revenue up 217%, Data Center compute up 244%, and networking up 133%, and attributes demand to enterprise software, consumer internet applications, and multiple industry verticals. Passage 111 gives Data Center revenue of $47.5 billion, the launch of AI inference platforms, DGX Cloud and AI Foundations, about 40% of Data Center revenue from AI inference, and large cloud providers as more than half of Q4 Data Center revenue. Passage 119 explains compute growth of 266% from higher Hopper GPU shipments for LLM training and inference and generative AI, and networking growth of 133% from InfiniBand shipments. Read together, these fully cover the requested growth drivers within the FY2024 filing scope.

Passage 000111 states that gross margin increased mainly because of Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue. Passage 000121 quantifies the inventory provision effect as unfavorable 2.7% in fiscal 2024 versus 7.5% in fiscal 2023. Together these fully support the requested change and its drivers. Passages 000054 and 000114 add only risk-factor and policy context. No requested element is missing.

Verified filing excerpts (extractive audit evidence; no derived calculations):

- Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% from fiscal year 2023. [NVDA-2024-10K-p000111](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/nvda-20240128.htm) (chunk: `000104581024000029#passage-000111`; accession: `0001045810-24-000029`).
- Revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $60.9 billion, up 126% from a year ago. Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was up 217%. [NVDA-2024-10K-p000110](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/nvda-20240128.htm) (chunk: `000104581024000029#passage-000110`; accession: `0001045810-24-000029`).
- Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2024, primarily driven by Data Center revenue growth and lower net inventory provisions as a percentage of revenue. [NVDA-2024-10K-p000111](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/nvda-20240128.htm) (chunk: `000104581024000029#passage-000111`; accession: `0001045810-24-000029`).
- The net effect on our gross margin from inventory provisions and sales of items previously written down was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% in fiscal year 2024 and 7.5% in fiscal year 2023. [NVDA-2024-10K-p000114](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/nvda-20240128.htm) (chunk: `000104581024000029#passage-000114`; accession: `0001045810-24-000029`).
- The net effect on our gross margin was an unfavorable impact of 2.7% and 7.5% in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively. [NVDA-2024-10K-p000121](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581024000029/nvda-20240128.htm) (chunk: `000104581024000029#passage-000121`; accession: `0001045810-24-000029`).
